help.title: Webhooks Guide
help.howDesc: When an event occurs, NodeAccess saves the delivery to a queue, signs the payload with HMAC-SHA256, and sends it via HTTP POST to your URL. On failure (5xx or timeout), retries are made with exponential backoff. After exhausting max retries, the delivery moves to Dead Letter and can be manually retried from the deliveries panel.

outbound.when: Use when NodeAccess needs to notify another system about something that happened inside the platform.

steps.target: Enter the public HTTPS URL of the system that will receive the events.
steps.events: Select only the events that make sense for the integration.
steps.security: Configure an HMAC secret so the receiver can validate the event origin.
steps.deliveries: Use the deliveries view to track success, failures, retries and manual resend.

practices.leastEvents: Start with a small event set and expand only when there is a real need.
practices.https: Prefer stable public HTTPS URLs; private addresses are blocked for security.
practices.hmac: Always validate the X-NodeAccess-Signature header in the receiving system.
practices.monitorFailures: Monitor failures and Dead Letter entries so important events are not missed.

inbound.when: Use when an external platform needs to inform NodeAccess about monitoring, inventory, incidents, approvals or operational context.

steps.endpoint: Create an inbound endpoint for the external provider, such as monitoring, cmdb or itsm.
steps.token: Copy the token URL at creation time and configure that URL in the sending system.
steps.signature: Configure an HMAC secret and send X-NodeAccess-Signature with an idempotency key.
steps.receipts: Track receipts to validate accepted, duplicate, rejected or signature error events.

practices.idempotency: Always send a unique idempotency key per external event.
practices.restrictEvents: Restrict accepted types, such as host.unavailable and host.recovered.
practices.protectToken: Treat the endpoint token as a technical credential and rotate it if exposed.
practices.noCriticalAutomation: Do not use inbound for automatic critical actions without a specific policy and use case.
